title: Legislative districts of San Jose del Monte

{{Short description|Legislative districts of the Philippines}} {{Politics of the Philippines}} [[File:Bulacan Congressional Districts 2022.svg|thumb|right|The congressional districts of Bulacan since 2022
{{small|{{legend|#white|Lone District of San Jose del Monte}}}}]] The '''legislative districts of San Jose del Monte''' are the representations of the [[Cities of the Philippines|component city]] of [[San Jose del Monte]] in the [[Congress of the Philippines]]. The city is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the Congress through its [[#Lone District|lone congressional district]]. == History == San Jose del Monte was represented as part of [[Bulacan]]'s [[Legislative districts of Bulacan#At-Large (1943–1944)|at-large district]] in the [[Malolos Congress]] (1898–1899) and the [[National Assembly (Second Philippine Republic)|National Assembly of the Second Philippine Republic]] (1943–1944) and the [[Bulacan's 2nd congressional district|second district]] from 1907 to 1941 and from 1945 to 1972. The province of Bulacan was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region III]] from 1978 to 1984, and elected [[Regular Batasang Pambansa#Members|four representatives]] at-large to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]]. San Jose del Monte was placed in the [[Bulacan's 4th congressional district|fourth district]] of Bulacan after the reorganization of the province's legislative districts under the new Constitution{{Cite web|url=http://www.lawphil.net/consti/cons1987.html|title = 1987 Philippine Constitution - the LawPhil Project}} which took effect on February 7, 1987. San Jose del Monte, which became a city in 2000, was separated from the fourth district of Bulacan on December 18, 2003 by virtue of Republic Act No. 9230{{cite PH act|chamber=RA|number=9230|url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/download/ra_12/RA09230.pdf |title=An Act amending section 10(b) and section 58 of Republic Act No. 8797, otherwise known as "An Act Converting The Municipality Of San Jose Del Monte, Bulacan Into A Component City To Be Known As The City Of San Jose Del Monte" and Providing Funds Therefor | date=18 December 2003 |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |access-date=12 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110629110211/http://www.congress.gov.ph/download/ra_12/RA09230.pdf |archive-date=29 June 2011 |url-status=dead}} which amended the city charter (Republic Act No. 8797){{cite PH act|chamber=RA|number=8797 |url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/download/ra_11/RA08797.pdf |title=An Act Converting The Municipality Of San Jose Del Monte, Bulacan Into A Component City To Be Known As The City Of San Jose Del Monte |date=15 July 2000|publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |access-date=12 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120402161403/http://www.congress.gov.ph/download/ra_11/RA08797.pdf |archive-date=2 April 2012 |url-status=dead}} authored by then Congressman [[Angelito Sarmiento]], and elected its own representative starting in the [[2004 Philippine general election|2004 elections]]. However, the city's residents still vote as part of the province's 4th ''Sangguniang Panlalawigan'' district for the purpose of electing [[Bulacan Provincial Board|Provincial Board]] members.[http://www.comelec.gov.ph/statistics/2010natl_local/summary%20by%20district/region3.html COMELEC - 2010 Districting - Region III]{{dead link|date=December 2017|bot=InternetArchiveBot|fix-attempted=yes}} == Lone District == {{columns-list|colwidth=10em| }} {| class="wikitable sortable" style="margin: 1em auto; font-size:100%; line-height:20px; text-align:center" |+Legislative districts and representatives of [[San Jose del Monte|San Jose Del Monte City]] ! rowspan="2" |District ! colspan="2" rowspan="2" |Current Representative ! colspan="4" |Party ! rowspan="2" |Constituent [[Administrative divisions of the Philippines|LGUs]] ! rowspan="2" |Area ! rowspan="2" |Population (2020) |- ! colspan="2" |Local ! colspan="2" |National |- ![[San Jose del Monte's at-large congressional district|Lone]] |[[File:Rep.
